lines.text: Today you become a text detective, cutting words apart and building the classic game of Hangman.
A string is a row of letters, and each one has an index starting at 0. city[0] is the first letter and city[-1] is the last. len(city) counts them all.
city[0:5] gives the letters from index 0 up to, but not including, index 5.
Leave a number out to start from the beginning or go to the end. city[::-1] gives the whole string backwards.
.upper(), .lower() and .title() change the capitals. .replace() swaps text, .count() counts it and .split() breaks a sentence into a list of words.
Each one makes a new string, because a string can never be changed.
"sam" in "samosa" is True, so in can search inside text. for letter in word: visits each letter in turn.
That is exactly what Hangman needs.
Index zero is the first letter, and minus one is the last letter.
The slice from zero to five gives five letters, stopping just before index five.
Title gives every word a capital letter, and replace swaps chai for lassi.
Count finds four letter a, and split breaks the sentence into a list of words.
The loop visits one letter at a time, from the first to the last.
Each time the letter is found inside the vowel string, we add one to the count.
This is the heart of Hangman: we show the letters already guessed.
Every other letter becomes an underscore, so the player sees the gaps.
Strings cannot be changed one letter at a time, so this line crashes.
Instead, build a new string, for example with word dot capitalize or by adding pieces together.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
